working-as-a-physicist: A newton, a joule, a watt: what are they actually made of?
electric-circuits: A lamp glows while charge flows through it. Does any of the charge get used up on the way?
materials: How could you test whether a crown is pure gold without damaging it?
waves-particle-nature-of-light: Sing a higher note. Does the sound reach the far side of the room any sooner?
further-mechanics: Why can a stunt performer walk away from a fall onto an airbag that would kill on concrete?
electric-magnetic-fields: Halve the distance between two charges. How many times bigger does the force between them get?
nuclear-particle-physics: Two atoms of the same element can have different masses. What is different inside them?
thermodynamics: In a cold room, metal feels colder than wood. Is it really at a lower temperature?
space: Two stars look equally bright in the night sky. How can we tell which one really gives out more light?
gravitational-fields: Astronauts float on the space station. How much weaker is Earth's gravity up there?
oscillations: Why does an oscillating mass on a spring move fastest at the one point where no overall force acts on it?
nuclear-radiation: Can a nucleus decay three times and end up as the same element it started as?
electric-and-magnetic-fields-part-2: A wire carrying a current lies between the poles of a magnet. Which way is it pushed?
electric-circuits-part-2: Stretch a metal wire to twice its length. What happens to its resistance?
mechanics-part-2: Can something be moving fast when all the forces on it cancel out?
mechanics-part-3: Can an object's balance point be in empty space, where there is no material at all?
nuclear-and-particle-physics-part-2: Charge and energy would both balance if a proton turned into a positron and light. So what forbids it?
waves-and-particle-nature-of-light-part-: You walk away from a small light source. How quickly does the light reaching you fade?
Turning one filter against another can block light, but not sound. What does that tell us about light?
Why can a few minutes of weak ultraviolet damage skin cells' DNA when hours of bright red light can't?
